seo_title: Find First Generation Scholarships in the USA
seo_description: First generation scholarships in the USA with deadlines, award ranges, and requirement signals. Compare listings and apply on official pages.
intro: Trying to find USA scholarships for first generation students usually means sorting through mixed eligibility rules, study levels, and subject areas before you can decide where to apply. This filtered slice brings those listings into one place so you can compare options that may fit high school seniors, current college students, graduate students, and some international or permanent resident applicants alongside US citizens. The programs below span themes like education, STEM, community, disability, arts, and other miscellaneous categories, so it is worth scanning beyond your major. Award amounts vary by listing, deadlines differ by program, and requirements are not identical. Many rows appear to have lighter application signals and often no essay, but you should still read each listing carefully and verify details on the official source before applying.
h1: Compare First Generation Scholarships in the USA
supporting: A smart way to use this list is to compare the requirement line, study level, residency wording, category tags, and deadline text side by side instead of judging a scholarship by title alone. Some first generation awards in this USA catalog may connect with education, business, arts, history, English, or science-related interests, while others are broader. If you want to apply in the current cycle, check dates promptly because some rows may close sooner than expected. Use the listing details to build a shortlist, then open the official page to confirm eligibility, materials, and the latest terms before you submit anything.

faq.question: How do I find first-generation scholarships in the USA that fit my situation?
faq.answer: Use this filtered view to compare eligibility, study level, field, amount, and deadline row by row. In this catalog slice, listings span levels from high school senior through graduate study, and official program pages are the place to confirm current rules.

faq.question: Can I apply if I’m an international student or permanent resident, not just a U.S. citizen?
faq.answer: Some listings in this USA scholarship catalog show citizenship or residency labels such as U.S. citizen, U.S. permanent resident, and international student. Check each row and then verify on the official source, because eligibility differs by program.

faq.question: What should I compare before I apply to first-generation scholarships?
faq.answer: Focus on the basics that vary across these rows: who qualifies, study level, field of study, award amount, and deadline. Amounts vary by listing, and deadlines differ by program, so confirm both on the official scholarship page before you apply.

faq.question: Are there first-generation scholarships here for specific majors or categories?
faq.answer: Yes—this filtered set includes listings tied to categories such as Education, STEM, Community, Disability, and Arts, with sample fields like education, English language and literature, visual and performing arts, business, and history. If you want to explore matches faster, compare the category and field labels on each row before opening the official listing.

faq.question: Are these first-generation scholarships usually quick to apply for?
faq.answer: Many listings in this catalog slice show a lighter requirement signal, and many sampled rows flag no essay, but that is not a guarantee for every program. Deadlines also vary by row, with at least some listings closing soon, so check the official page promptly before you start an application.
